q: What calorific value does India use for natural gas per SCM?
title: Natural gas GCV per SCM in India
short: PPAC's gas conversions, sourced from GAIL, use a gross calorific value of 10,000 kcal per SCM, with net calorific value at 90% of that. One MMBtu equals 25.2 SCM on this basis. Domestic production averages 8,000 to 9,480 kcal per SCM, so use the GCV on your own bill when it is printed.
audience: Factories on piped natural gas, CGD customers

ul: 1 SCM = 1 cubic metre at 1 atmosphere and 15.56 C.
Gross calorific value: 10,000 kcal per SCM. Net calorific value: 90% of GCV.
1 MMBtu = 25.2 SCM at 10,000 kcal per SCM; 1 MMBtu = 252,000 kcal.
Density of gas: 0.76 kg per SCM; specific gravity 0.62.
Average natural gas production in India: 8,000 to 9,480 kcal per SCM (Table 9.1).

ol: Multiply SCM by the GCV on your bill, or 10,000 kcal if none is printed.
Take 90% for net calorific value and convert to GJ (1 kcal = 4.19 kJ per PPAC).
Multiply by the IPCC natural gas default of 56.1 kg CO2 per GJ.

p: On these PPAC values one SCM works out to about 2.12 kg CO2, while 0.76 kg per SCM times the IPCC per-kg factor gives about 2.05. The two reference values imply slightly different gas. A bill that prints GCV settles it for your supply.
